newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk says combine's gas supply back to normal.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk says combine's gas supply back to normal.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group said natural gas supplies to its flagship metals plant had returned to normal after being cut by nearly a third for several weeks in June, group spokesman Sergei Vetchinin said on Tuesday.
"I wouldn't say that all the problems have been solved," he said. "But the main thing is that I can confirm that the combine is getting normal gas supplies."
Vetchinin said Norilsk had avoided significant disruptions to output by dipping into fuel oil stocks to fire plants when gas supplies fell.
Norilskgazprom cut gas supplies to 11 million cubic metres per day in early June from 16 million over unpaid gas debts.

Vetchinin said further talks between Norilsk, the lead plant of the RAO Norilsky Nikel group, and Norilskgazprom were needed to resolve the problem. Norilskgazprom says the financially-troubled plant, based in the Arctic town of Norilsk, owes it 1.9 trillion roubles ($330 million).

The Krasnoyarsk regional arbitration court, which has jurisdiction over the plant, said on Tuesday it may consider starting bankruptcy proceedings against the plant later this month, prompted by complaints from Norilskgazprom.
